newsitem.title: QATAR: INDIAN DEMAND FOR LNG TO GROW - GAIL.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN DEMAND FOR LNG TO GROW - GAIL.

text.p: Indian LNG import demand will reach an annual five million tonnes in 2005 and 10 million tonnes in 2010, an Indian gas planner said on Tuesday.
R. Sharma, executive director of marketing and planning at Gas Authority of India (GAIL), also told delegates at a gas conference in Qatar that India faced a growing gas supply gap.
Rising local power demand would push this shortfall to 78 million cubic metres a day by 1999-2000, rising again to 215 million cubic metres by 2009-2010, Sharma said.
Indian demand was forecast to rise to 146 million cubic metres in 1999-2000 and 283 million cubic metres in 2009-2010, from 89 million cubic metres in 1996-1997.
Gas supply projects from Oman and Iran remained hampered by technical and political obstacles, maintaining India's interest in 14 LNG schemes in the Mideast Gulf and other regions.
U.S.-based Enron Corp is in negotiations with Qatar to set up an LNG plant in the Gulf Arab state to supply its Dabhol power plant in India and the Gujarat Gas Corp with LNG from 2001.
